title: Damped driven oscillator
tagline: Friction, a motor and resonance: when to push to go higher.

block.title: Block
block.desc: Its mass m is inertia: how hard it is to accelerate (F = m ẍ). More mass → slower oscillation, and the damper slows it less.

spring.title: Spring
spring.desc: Restoring force proportional to the stretch, F = −k x. Stiffer → higher natural frequency ω₀ = √(k/m).

damper.title: Damper
damper.desc: A piston in a fluid: a force opposing the velocity, F = −b ẋ. Water for low b, oil for medium b, honey for high b.

motor.title: Crank motor
motor.desc: Pushes and pulls with F₀ cos(ω t). The crank radius shows the amplitude F₀/k and turns at ω. When ω nears ω₀: resonance!

wall.title: Frame
wall.desc: Fixed structure holding the motor and the damper tube. It never moves.

velocity.title: Velocity
velocity.desc: The arrow shows the velocity v. While paused, drag its tip to choose v₀.

presetInfo.undamped: No friction, no motor (b = 0, F₀ = 0). Energy is conserved: it oscillates forever with the same amplitude at ω₀ = √(k/m).
presetInfo.underdamped: Light friction (γ = b/2m < ω₀). It still oscillates, but the amplitude decays as e^(−γt) and the frequency drops a little: ω_d = √(ω₀² − γ²).
presetInfo.critical: γ = ω₀. Returns to equilibrium as fast as possible without overshooting or oscillating: what a car's shock absorbers aim for.
presetInfo.overdamped: γ > ω₀. So much friction that it no longer oscillates: it creeps back to equilibrium, more slowly than in the critical case.
presetInfo.resonance: The motor pushes at the system's natural rhythm (ω = ω_res ≈ ω₀). Every push adds energy and the amplitude grows until the damper dissipates what the motor supplies.
presetInfo.beats: No friction and ω close to ω₀. The free and the driven oscillations add up and interfere: the amplitude swells and fades with period 2π/|ω₀ − ω|.
